label.en: emplyee insurance (maximum dagloon)

description.en: This constant is the statutory maximum daily wage ("maximum dagloon") applied under the Dutch employee-insurance schemes (werknemersverzekeringen), capping the reference earnings used to compute earnings-related benefits. In the model it is used in bma_nl/BenCalc as the Comp_UpLim parameter to cap the previous income underlying the pregnancy/childbirth allowance, which per the Country Report pays 100% of the daily wage up to this maximum. It is also used in bunct_nl/BenCalc (comp_perElig) to cap the previous earnings on which the unemployment benefit (75% of previous wage, falling to 70% after two months) is calculated. The value is uprated annually - from EUR 290.67/day in 2025 (per the bunct.md Country Report table) to EUR 304.25/day in the model's latest (2026) system.

description.en: Labelled 'maximum premieloon' (maximum premium wage), this constdef_nl constant appears to represent an annual ceiling on wages subject to Dutch employee social-insurance ('werknemersverzekeringen') contributions — conceptually the same type of cap the Country Report reports for employer unemployment- and disability-insurance contributions (the 'uplim'/'Maxbase2' figures in the ersic_nl section, about €6,322/month ≈ €75,864/year in the 2025 system). This constant's own value (€79,409, from a series of 21 dated values since 2006) is plausibly a further-uprated version of that same type of wage ceiling for a later system year. However, it is not referenced by any function in the scanned spine or add-ons (0 usage sites), so it appears to be an unused/legacy constant rather than one actively driving current calculations, and its precise role could not be confirmed from available sources.

description.en: $MinWage_m as defined in the country's central constants policy (constdef_nl) represents the monthly gross statutory minimum wage, with a comment added at EUROMOD version 11.4 noting this instance specifically as the variant excluding the 8% holiday allowance. In the current NL model this defining instance is not populated for the latest date (recorded value is "n/a"); the live figure under the same constant name is instead supplied by the parallel $MinWage_m defined in policy yem_nl (id 48, currently EUR 2,294.40/month). Through this shared name the constant feeds four spine calculations: bma_nl's BenCalc (parameter Comp_perTU) sets the monthly Pregnancy and Childbirth Allowance for self-employed claimants equal to the minimum wage (per the country report, "for self-employed, the benefit equals the minimum wage"); poa_nl's ArithOp uses 15% of it as the earnings disregard in the flat-rate State Pension (AOW)'s means test on a younger spouse's income; psu_nl's ArithOp uses 50% of it as the earnings disregard in the Survivor Benefit (ANW) income test; and yem_nl's own ArithOp combines it with a holiday-allowance rate to build a minimum-wage-plus-holiday-allowance figure.

description.en: $PenAge ('Pension Age', latest 67) is the statutory state pension age (AOW-leeftijd), one of the most widely reused constants in the Dutch model, defined centrally in constdef_nl and consumed at 61 sites across the spine. It sets the household-age-group boundaries (A/C/E/G) for rent-allowance eligibility and calculation in bho_nl (literally 'dag<$PenAge' / 'dag>=$PenAge' per bho.md), is the qualifying age for the flat-rate state pension described in poa.md ('all residents who have reached the state pension age'), delimits the age-dependent net-to-gross conversion factors for social assistance in bsagross_nl/bsasegross_nl (Table 2.10 in bsagross.md), sets the #_AgeMin/#_AgeMax age bounds for social-assistance benefit rates in bsanet_nl/bsasenet_nl, and is referenced directly in tin_nl to determine eligibility for the old-age tax credit ('taxpayers aged above the state pension age ($PenAge)'). It is also used in bhlmt_nl (sickness benefit) and TransLMA_nl (labour-market transition eligibility).

description.en: This constant is the minimum number of days (52 days, roughly one working year) that must have been worked within a calendar year for that year to count toward the employment record required for the extended (earnings-related) unemployment benefit. Per the Country Report (bunct.md), extended-benefit eligibility requires having worked 52 days or more during at least four of the last five years, on top of the general 26-weeks-in-36 test; this constant supplies the 52-day per-year threshold. It is used, together with $eUB_QperTot (the 4-of-5-years/48-month condition), in bunct_nl/Elig's elig_cond parameter, which forms the extended-benefit eligibility check in the spine.

The bunct.md Country Report describes this as an additional condition, on top of the general 26-out-of-36-weeks test, for entitlement to the longer, earnings-related extended benefit. In the model it is used in bunct_nl/ArithOp's formula parameter to compute the number of days worked in the qualifying period, and in bunct_nl/Elig's elig_cond parameter as part of the extended-benefit eligibility check, both in the spine.

description.en: This constant is the standard (non-elevated) upper limit of the Dutch income-tax/peoples'-insurance 'band 1' — the ceiling on the first tax bracket and on the maximum base for AOW/ANW/WLZ peoples' insurance contributions that applies to the general population (defined in constdef_nl). It is used in InitVar_nl's BenCalc as a comp_perTU component amount, added once for tax units whose members do not meet the elevated-cohort age condition captured by $tin_lim1lft; the counterpart component for that older cohort uses $tin_bandlim1a instead. The Country Report shows this same limit (Table 2.28 'band 1 up to'; Table 2.24 'pi_maxbase') at €38,441 for the 2025 system, so this constant's later value of €38,883 is consistent with a further year of annual uprating of that identical threshold.

It feeds into InitVar_nl's BenCalc as the comp_perTU value of the component whose eligibility condition uses the age threshold $tin_lim1lft, so members of this older cohort are assigned the higher ceiling rather than the standard one. The Country Report documents the same distinction (Table 2.28 'band1 (born before 1-1-1946)' = €40,502 in 2025; Table 2.24 'pi_maxbase when born before 1-1-1946' = €40,502), so this constant's later value of €41,123 is consistent with continued annual uprating of that grandfathered threshold.

description.en: $tin_bandlim2 is an annual income threshold used as the Base of the tin_nl/SchedCalc that computes 'Additional income tax (limitation mortgage interest deduction)' — the surcharge that caps mortgage-interest relief below the top marginal rate. Its latest modelled value (€78,426/year) sits just above the Country Report's 'Band2 up to' figure in Table 2.28 (€76,817 in 2025, the point from which the 49.5% top rate applies), consistent with the CR's account of the deduction limitation only biting once income enters the top Box 1 bracket. Per the Country Report, since 2014 the effective mortgage-interest deduction rate for top-bracket taxpayers has been reduced annually via this additional tax (e.g. rising to 12.45% by 2023), and $tin_bandlim2 marks the income level at which this limitation starts to apply.

description.en: $MinWage_m as defined in policy yem_nl is the monthly gross statutory minimum wage; its latest recorded value is EUR 2,294.40 (raw "2294.40#m"), part of a series of 21 dated observations starting 2006-01-01 that tracks successive statutory upratings of the minimum wage. Per the Country Report (Table 2.4), this base rate is €286.45 per quarter per child as of 2025 and has been periodically uprated since the benefit was first modelled from 2006-01-01, when it stood at €177.89 per quarter (per the parameter label); the latest modelled value is €295.07 per quarter. In the bfa_nl policy it is used in an ArithOp formula whose comment marks it as the '2006' calculation for children over 12, i.e. an early version of the age-band amount computation that was later generalised via the age multipliers $bfa_mult1/$bfa_mult2/$bfa_mult3 (CR Table 2.5), which the label states are all applied on top of this same base figure.

description.en: Defined in tpcpe_nl (occupational pension contributions — the Country Report's Direct Taxes section notes that tpcpe is deducted, alongside the employee unemployment-insurance contribution, from employment and self-employment income when computing taxable 'income from work' for the income-tax work credit), this constant is the lower boundary of the pensionable-salary base, i.e. the 'franchise' below which no occupational pension contribution is due (mirroring the portion of pay already covered by the state pension, AOW). It is entered into tpcpe_nl's SchedCalc as a Band_UpLim, forming the ceiling of the schedule's untaxed first band, with contributions only levied on pay between this threshold (€17,367) and the higher cap $tpcpe_base_uplim, at the rate $tpcpe_ee_avgRate.

description.en: Defined in tpcpe_nl, this constant is the upper boundary of the pensionable-salary base used to compute occupational pension contributions — the Country Report's Direct Taxes section identifies tpcpe as the occupational pension contribution deducted from work income for income-tax purposes. It is entered into tpcpe_nl's SchedCalc as a Band_UpLim, capping the schedule's contribution-bearing band at €137,800: pay between the lower franchise $tpcpe_base_lowlim and this cap is charged the rate $tpcpe_ee_avgRate, while pay above the cap accrues no further contribution.

description.en: Defined in tpcpe_nl, this constant is the average employee contribution rate (6.19% in the latest system) applied to the occupational-pension pensionable-salary band. It is entered into tpcpe_nl's SchedCalc as the Band_Rate for the band running from the franchise $tpcpe_base_lowlim to the cap $tpcpe_base_uplim, so contributions equal this rate multiplied by the portion of pay falling within that band. Because Dutch occupational pension schemes vary by employer and sector, EUROMOD uses this single average rate (as flagged by its name 'avgRate') as a simplifying approximation rather than modelling scheme-specific rates; the Country Report's Direct Taxes section confirms tpcpe (occupational pension contributions) is deducted from work income in the income-tax calculation.

description.en: $psu_base is the maximum monthly base amount of the Dutch survivor benefit (Algemene Nabestaandenwet, ANW), inclusive of the holiday allowance and the extra allowance granted since 2007 (Country Report Table 2.7, 'Total' row). It is used in the psu_nl policy's ArithOp function (comment 'Calculation and means-test') as the full pre-means-tested benefit amount, from which the income-tested reduction for earnings/private-pension income above the disregard is then subtracted. The survivor benefit is paid monthly to a surviving spouse/partner below the state pension age who has an unmarried child under 18 or is at least 45% disabled for work; the CR reports a 2025 total of EUR 1,717.38 (EUR 1,573.58 base + EUR 122.64 holiday allowance + EUR 21.16 extra allowance), consistent with the model's uprated 2026 value of EUR 1,796.67. The benefit is taxable and counts as income in means tests for other benefits.

description.en: $tschl_prem_av is the national average annual flat-rate premium (nominale premie) that residents pay for compulsory basic health insurance under the Zorgverzekeringswet (ZVW/Health Insurance Act). It is used in tschl_nl/BenCalc as the comp_perTU component labelled 'Flat rate health insurance contribution', adding this amount once per tax unit to compute the flat-rate part of the household's health insurance liability. As the Country Report explains, EUROMOD approximates the actual (insurer-specific) flat premium with this single national average, since real premiums vary between insurance companies and individuals are free to choose their insurer; for context, the reported average flat premium (tschlfx_s) was €1,905 per adult (aged 18+) per year in 2025. The constant is updated for each system year to track the evolving nationwide average premium.

In tschl_nl/SchedCalc it is the band_rate for 'Earnings-related health insurance contribution - part 1' (the wage/benefit component, tschl01_s); it also feeds bsagross_nl's ArithOp and BenCalc, where it is added back to gross up net social assistance income into its gross equivalent for tax/contribution purposes (see bsagross.md). Per the Country Report this is the higher of the two ZVW rates (charged on 'earnings etc.'); Table 2.25 shows it falling from 6.75% in 2022 to 6.51% in 2025, applied up to a maximum contribution base of €75,860 in 2025.

description.en: $tin_deduc_se ('taxdeduction selfemployed', latest €1,200/year) is the flat self-employment tax allowance ('zelfstandigenaftrek'), used as the band_amount in tin_nl/SchedCalc for 'Self-employment tax allowance: entitlement'. It matches the declining trend in the Country Report's Table 2.26, which shows 'amt_1' falling from €6,310 (2022) to €5,030 (2023), €3,750 (2024) and €2,470 (2025) under a legislated multi-year phase-down of the allowance; the constant continues this trend to a later modelled value. The Country Report's tax-base section (Box 3) states that 'starting in 2016, the additional asset allowance for persons above the state pension age ... has been abolished', which matches this constant's near-static history (only one recorded change since 2006) — consistent with the parameter being frozen once the scheme stopped applying, and retained mainly so EUROMOD can reproduce pre-2016 systems. The CR does not give the exact historical asset limit, so the specific figure is not independently confirmed.

Per the country report (Table 2.24), the ANW rate is the smallest of the three components - 0.1% throughout 2022-2025 - payable by all Box-1 taxpayers regardless of employment status.

description.en: Income threshold B used in the child-related budget's taper formula 'C − D × max(0, income − B)', applied when the recipient tax unit is a single parent (no fiscal partner). It is consumed in chall_nl/BenCalc's comp_perTU parameter, which computes the income- and age-related child allowance (the post-2008 replacement for the child tax credit) for the tax unit, where 'income' is total taxable income in Box 1 and Box 3 (i_taxabley_box1 + i_taxbase_box3). Below this threshold the tax unit receives the full base amount C (plus any age increases or single-parent supplement); above it, the entitlement is reduced by D per euro of excess income. The Country Report shows this single-parent threshold rising from €22,356 (2022) to €28,406 (2025) and notes that since 2020 it has been set lower than the couples' threshold ($chall_B2); the model's latest value is €29,736/year.

description.en: Represents the marginal rate 'A' applied to the portion of total taxable income exceeding threshold B in the norm-premium formula used to calculate the Dutch health care allowance (zorgtoeslag). It is used in bhlmt_nl's BenCalc function (parameter comp_perTU, function comment 'Calculate norm premium') as the coefficient multiplying max(0, taxable income − B). Per the Country Report, norm premium = A·max(0, income − B) + C·(with allowance partner) + D·(without partner); Table 2.18 shows A rising from about 13.61% (2022) to 13.70% (2025), consistent with this constant's most recent recorded value of roughly 13.73%.

description.en: This constant is the (average) employer contribution rate to disability insurance (arbeidsongeschiktheidsverzekering), expressed as a fraction of gross wage rather than a percentage (e.g. the latest recorded value corresponds to 7.91%). It is used in ersic_NL/SchedCalc as the band_rate parameter for the schedule computing the 'Employer contribution to disability insurance' (tscerdi_s), multiplying wages up to the ceiling set by $ersic_uplim to derive the amount employers must pay. Per the Country Report, employers of private-sector staff below the state pension age pay, on average, a single contribution rate on wages up to a monthly ceiling, even though since 2022 the actual Dutch scheme differentiates a higher rate for large employers and a lower rate for small employers (paying less than 25 times the average wage) - EUROMOD models this with one averaged rate. The rate has risen over time (from about 7.11% in 2022 to 7.545% in 2025 per the Country Report's Table 2.23), consistent with this parameter's 20 recorded values since 2006.

It is used in ersic_NL/SchedCalc as the band_rate parameter for the schedule computing the 'Employer contribution to unemployment insurance' (tscerui_s), applied to wages up to the ceiling defined by $ersic_uplim. Since 2020 the actual scheme differentiates a low rate for employees on permanent contracts and a high rate for those on temporary/flexible contracts, but because the underlying data cannot reliably distinguish contract type, EUROMOD instead uses a single blended national-average rate - reported by the Country Report as 3.25% in 2022, 3.19% in 2023, 3.89% in 2024 and 3.29% in 2025.

It is used in ersic_NL/SchedCalc as the band_uplim parameter for the 'Employer contribution to disability insurance' schedule, capping the wage base so that the contribution rate ($ersic_disab_r) only applies up to this ceiling - the Country Report gives the calculation as 0.07545*min(wage, ceiling), with the ceiling equal to EUR 6,322 per month in 2025. The specific legal basis is not documented in the available Country Report, which covers the rent-allowance system only through 2025 and does not describe the 2026 reform.

description.en: Defines the maximum actual monthly rent above which a household is entitled to no rent allowance at all. It carries a concrete value only for 2025 (€900.07); the constant is n/a for 2008-2024 and n/a again from 2026 onward, when the equivalent role is taken over by the system-2026 constant $bho_rentlim. It is used in bho_nl's Elig function as part of the general eligibility condition (elig_cond, comment 'General elibility condition'), and it matches the Country Report's 'up_rent_lt' threshold, which states that no subsidy is awarded when 'actual rent [is] above €900.07 (up_rent_lt)'.

description.en: A monthly rent floor for household group A (single persons under state pension age) in bho_nl's pre-2026 rent-allowance calculation, valued at €192.00 in 2024 and €199.05 in 2025. It is used both as the 'lowlim' (lower limit) argument in the ArithOp step computing group A's norm rent (comment 'Household A: calculation of norm rent (2008)') and within the group-A Elig eligibility condition (comment 'Household A: eligibility'). The Country Report describes a 'minimum norm rent' floor below which the norm rent used in the subsidy formula cannot fall, but its published Table 2.14 figures for these years (€226.67 in 2024, €236.19 in 2025) are noticeably higher and instead match the separate, currently unused constant $hbo_minnormA — so while $hbo_minbasA clearly performs the operative floor/eligibility role in the model, its exact relationship to the Report's published minimum-rent figures could not be fully reconciled from the available sources.

description.en: This is the lower annual household-income breakpoint (household disposable income, ils_dispy; EUR 56,412/year from 2026, up from EUR 38,802 in 2024 and EUR 54,221 in 2025) in the income-tested compensation-rate schedule that policy xcc_nl applies to the second and any further dependent child (query IsDepChild & IsNtoMchild#2, i.e. child rank 2 and above among children aged 0-4 in formal daycare) when computing the Dutch childcare-cost compensation. In xcc_nl's second BenCalc component (function comment 'Childcare benefit'), households with income at or below this threshold get a compensation rate from the formula $bccfc_child2_base1 + $bccfc_child2_coef1*income (bounded between $bccfc_child2_minrate and the 96% ceiling $bccfc_maxrate); once income exceeds this threshold and up to $bccfc_child2_thres2, a flat rate ($bccfc_child2_flat) applies instead. The resulting rate is multiplied by the assumed childcare cost (xcc_s, built from $xcc_amt in the same policy's 'Costs' component) to give the modelled compensation amount (output bccfc_s), reflecting the income-tapered, child-rank-differentiated design of the Dutch childcare-fee allowance (kinderopvangtoeslag-style).

classification.reason: Income threshold for child care cost support policy

description.en: This is the upper annual household-income breakpoint (household disposable income, ils_dispy; EUR 65,695/year from 2026, versus EUR 67,479 in 2024 and EUR 63,144 in 2025) in the same second-child compensation-rate schedule of policy xcc_nl. Between $bccfc_child2_thres1 and this threshold, a flat rate ($bccfc_child2_flat) applies to the childcare-cost compensation for the second and any further dependent child (BenCalc, function comment 'Childcare benefit'); once household income exceeds this threshold, the rate switches back to a formula, $bccfc_child2_base2 + $bccfc_child2_coef2*income, again bounded between $bccfc_child2_minrate and the 96% ceiling $bccfc_maxrate. As with thres1, the resulting rate multiplies the assumed childcare cost (xcc_s, from $xcc_amt) to yield the modelled compensation output bccfc_s, part of the income-tested Dutch childcare-fee allowance (kinderopvangtoeslag-style) design, which treats the second and subsequent children more generously than the first (which instead uses a single threshold, $bccfc_child1_thres).

classification.reason: Income threshold for child care cost support policy

description.en: Assumed standard weekly cost of formal childcare per eligible child (EUR 400/week, unchanged since 2024). It is used in xcc_nl's first BenCalc component (function comment 'Costs') as the Comp_perElig amount added once for every eligible child meeting the condition 'dag 0-4 & dccfc=1' (aged 0 to 4 and recorded/flagged as using formal daycare); an inline parameter comment in the model notes the figure assumes a standard 40-hour working week of care. This produces the output variable xcc_s, the imputed weekly childcare cost per child, which the policy's second BenCalc component ('Childcare benefit') then multiplies by income- and child-rank-tested compensation rates (built from the $bccfc_* family of constants, e.g. $bccfc_child2_thres1/thres2 for the second and later children) to compute the modelled childcare-fee compensation (bccfc_s) - EUROMOD's approximation of the Dutch childcare allowance (kinderopvangtoeslag).

classification.reason: Child care benefit amount per week set by policy
